checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-017: Is compute_requests_hash deterministic across all execution client implementations?

reachability.notes: Different hash outputs across clients cause block rejection at the CL, preventing finalization.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the compute_requests_hash implementation in the target execution client. 2. Prepare a canonical set of test requests with known expected hash outputs. 3. Verify the two-level SHA-256 construction: (a) Each request is hashed individually, (b) Individual digests are fed into the outer hash in correct order. 4. Test with identical inputs across multiple execution client implementations (e.g., Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon). 5. Verify byte-level determinism: same input bytes MUST produce identical hash output. 6. Test edge cases: empty request lists, single request, maximum request count. 7. Verify request ordering is handled identically (requests must be processed in the same order). 8. Check for any floating-point operations or non-deterministic system calls in the hash computation path. 9. Attempt to craft inputs that could trigger implementation-specific behavior (e.g., encoding differences, padding variations).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0053, Trust Boundary: tb-017, Source Assumption: asm-029, Source Threat: stride-tampering-tb-017. PoC requirement: demonstrate that two client implementations produce different requests_hash for identical input. This is a consensus-critical invariant - any deviation causes CL-EL disagreement and prevents block finalization across the network.

checklist.title: Verify SHA-256 Two-Level Construction Correctness in compute_requests_hash

reachability.notes: Different hash outputs across clients cause block rejection at the CL, preventing finalization.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the implementation of the two-level SHA-256 construction. 2. Verify Step 1: Each individual request is hashed using SHA-256 to produce a 32-byte digest. 3. Verify Step 2: All individual digests are concatenated in the correct order and fed into the outer SHA-256 hash. 4. Check that no additional data (padding, length prefixes, separators) is incorrectly added between digests. 5. Verify the order of requests is well-defined and matches the specification. 6. Test with reference vectors from the specification if available. 7. Manually compute expected hash output for test vectors and compare with implementation output.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0053. Supporting check for the two-level hash construction correctness. Incorrect implementation of the hash construction would cause cross-client incompatibility.

checklist.title: Verify Request Serialization Determinism at CL-EL Boundary

reachability.notes: Different hash outputs across clients cause block rejection at the CL, preventing finalization.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify how requests are serialized before hashing at the CL-EL boundary. 2. Verify serialization is canonical (no alternative encodings for same data). 3. Check for endianness consistency across implementations. 4. Verify string encoding (UTF-8) is handled identically. 5. Check numeric field encoding (big-endian vs little-endian, fixed-width vs variable-width). 6. Test with requests containing edge-case values: zero values, maximum values, empty fields. 7. Verify no implementation-specific serialization quirks (e.g., different JSON libraries producing different byte sequences).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0053. Supporting check ensuring the data fed into compute_requests_hash is deterministic. Non-deterministic serialization would cause hash divergence even with correct hash implementation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-019: Is EIP-7702 authorization properly validated for cross-chain and same-chain replay protection?

reachability.notes: An attacker can capture a valid authorization and replay it on another chain or after a nonce increment.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the EIP-7702 authorization processing entry points in the execution client. 2. Verify that chain_id is included in the authorization payload and validated against the current chain. 3. Verify that nonce is included and checked against the authorizer's current nonce. 4. Capture a valid EIP-7702 authorization and attempt to replay it on a different chain (e.g., mainnet vs testnet) - verify rejection. 5. Capture a valid authorization and wait for the authorizer's nonce to increment, then attempt replay - verify rejection. 6. Verify ECDSA signature verification is performed before any state changes. 7. Check for any code paths that bypass chain_id or nonce validation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054, Trust Boundary: tb-019, Source Threat: stride-tampering-tb-019, Source Assumption: asm-026. PoC: capture a valid EIP-7702 authorization and replay it on a different chain or after nonce changes.

checklist.title: Verify Execution Client Authorization Handling: Does actor-execution-client properly reject replayed EIP-7702 authorizations?

reachability.notes: An attacker can capture a valid authorization and replay it on another chain or after a nonce increment.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the authorization validation logic in the execution client codebase. 2. Trace the code path from transaction receipt to authorization processing. 3. Verify chain_id comparison uses strict equality against the current chain's ID. 4. Verify nonce comparison uses the authorizer account's current on-chain nonce. 5. Ensure validation failures result in transaction rejection before any state modification. 6. Check for time-of-check-time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerabilities between nonce check and state update. 7. Verify error handling does not leak information about why authorization failed.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054. Supporting check for actor-execution-client node coverage.

checklist.title: Verify Authorizer Account Protection: Is actor-authorizer protected from unauthorized code delegation via replay?

reachability.notes: An attacker can capture a valid authorization and replay it on another chain or after a nonce increment.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Understand the authorizer's role in EIP-7702 - they sign authorizations to delegate code to their account. 2. Verify that a signed authorization can only be used once per nonce value. 3. Verify that an authorization signed for chain X cannot be used on chain Y. 4. Test edge cases: authorization with nonce=0, authorization with max nonce value, authorization with chain_id=0. 5. Verify that after successful authorization use, the authorizer's nonce is incremented atomically. 6. Check if there are any recovery mechanisms that could reset nonces and enable replay. 7. Test authorization revocation scenarios - can a used authorization be re-enabled?
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054. Supporting check for actor-authorizer node coverage.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-020: Is storage_root parameter validated before encode_account processes it?

reachability.notes: The caller must ensure storage_root correctness. An internal bug could provide an incorrect root.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all callers of encode_account function that pass storage_root parameter. 2. For each caller, verify that storage_root is computed as a valid 32-byte Merkle root of the account's storage trie before being passed. 3. Trace the data flow from storage trie operations to encode_account invocation to ensure no intermediate corruption. 4. Verify that no code path allows an attacker-influenced value to reach storage_root without proper validation. 5. Check for any edge cases where storage_root could be zero, truncated, or otherwise malformed. 6. Audit state synchronization paths to ensure storage_root is correctly derived during block processing.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0055, Trust Boundary: tb-020, Source Assumption: asm-022, Source Threat: stride-tampering-tb-020. CONDITIONAL SCOPE: Requires further investigation - this property is internal-only and depends on caller correctness. An internal bug providing incorrect storage_root would corrupt state trie and cause consensus divergence.

checklist.title: Verify caller-side validation: Do all encode_account callers correctly compute storage_root from account storage trie?

reachability.notes: The caller must ensure storage_root correctness. An internal bug could provide an incorrect root.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Enumerate all call sites to encode_account in the codebase. 2. For each call site, verify the storage_root computation follows the correct Merkle trie algorithm. 3. Check that the storage_root is always 32 bytes (not truncated or padded incorrectly). 4. Verify that empty storage tries produce the correct empty root hash. 5. Test edge cases: new accounts, accounts with cleared storage, accounts undergoing state transition. 6. Validate that concurrent access to storage trie during root computation is properly synchronized.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0055. Supporting check for boundary edge tb-020. Since encode_account DOES NOT validate storage_root, all callers must be audited to ensure they provide correct values.

checklist.title: Verify State Trie Integrity: Is actor-state-trie protected from corruption via incorrect storage_root values?

reachability.notes: The caller must ensure storage_root correctness. An internal bug could provide an incorrect root.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify how actor-state-trie stores and retrieves account data including storage_root. 2. Verify that storage_root values in the state trie are always derived from the actual storage trie contents. 3. Check for any code paths where storage_root could become desynchronized from actual storage. 4. Test state trie reconstruction scenarios to ensure storage_root consistency is maintained. 5. Verify that state trie snapshots and rollbacks preserve storage_root integrity. 6. Check for race conditions between storage updates and storage_root computation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0055. Supporting check for actor-state-trie node coverage. Protects against consensus divergence caused by incorrect storage_root values.

checklist.title: Can type alias byte-length constraints be bypassed at construction time?

reachability.notes: If type alias length enforcement is weak, malformed data could propagate through the system.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all constructors/factory functions for Address, Root, VersionedHash, and Bloom types. 2. Attempt to construct an Address with byte length != 20 (e.g., 19 or 21 bytes). 3. Attempt to construct a Root/VersionedHash with byte length != 32 (e.g., 31 or 33 bytes). 4. Attempt to construct a Bloom with byte length != 256 (e.g., 255 or 257 bytes). 5. Verify that all invalid constructions are rejected with appropriate errors. 6. Check for alternative construction paths (deserialization, type casting, unsafe operations) that might bypass validation. 7. If invalid instances can be created, trace their propagation through the system to identify downstream impacts.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0057, Source Assumption: asm-027. Invariant: Type aliases (Address=Bytes20, Root=Hash32, VersionedHash=Hash32, Bloom=Bytes256) MUST enforce byte-length constraints at construction time. PoC target: construct an Address with len != 20 and demonstrate it is accepted by the type system.
